SELECTED_INDEX: 6
CONFIDENCE: 0.47
EXPLANATION: Key experimental features are:  
• Strong C=O stretch at 1719 cm⁻¹ (matches aldehyde C=O 1720 cm⁻¹).  
• Conjugated C=C stretch at 1643 cm⁻¹ (characteristic of α,β-unsaturated carbonyls).  
• Two high-intensity C–H stretches in the 2930–2990 cm⁻¹ region plus an olefinic C–H near 3115 cm⁻¹ (expected for a molecule containing both sp² and sp³ C–H).  
• Distinct band at 2740 cm⁻¹, typical of the formyl (–CHO) C–H Fermi-resonance overtone found only in aldehydes.  
Among the candidates, only molecule 6 (C/C=C(\C=O)CC), an α,β-unsaturated aldehyde, simultaneously possesses an aldehydic C=O, a C=C bond, and an aldehydic hydrogen to account for the 2740 cm⁻¹ band, while also providing the requisite aliphatic and vinylic C–H stretches and mid-frequency bends (1407, 1454 cm⁻¹). Ketone, ester, acid, thioester, amide or CF₃-containing alternatives (candidates 1–5, 7–10) lack the aldehyde C–H stretch and are less consistent with the observed 2740 cm⁻¹ feature.
